$doc: Launch film v5: the rewritten Keeper script (docs/KEEPER_VOICE_GUIDE.md). Same picture and pacing as v4; the Keeper gets a name, a running bet on you, a running gag (Arjun) and an ending. A phrase either comes from v4 ({from, i}: same words, same frames, same lip-sync: the close-ups and the typed tagline are locked) or is new ({caption, at, dur}: designed against the picture, `at` on the film clock). `say` is what ElevenLabs reads when it differs from the caption; `eleven` is the line ready to paste, tags included. design_vo.py turns this into video/src/data/vo5.json.

S01.direction: The first thing anyone hears. Relaxed authority, as if he's been waiting for you; a flick of disdain on "quit". Not sleepy.
S01.eleven: [deadpan] Every habit app lets you quit.

S02.direction: "This one" turns toward you, unhurried. Beat. "bills you." lands with quiet satisfaction, savouring "bills". Underplay it.
S02.eleven: This one... [dry, quietly pleased] bills you.

S03.direction: A grand welcome over the drop, and he's clearly enjoying himself. Then he introduces himself mid-wave, proud of the title.
S03.eleven: [grandly, enjoying himself] Welcome to Kept. ... [proudly] I'm the Keeper.

S04.direction: A bouncer at the door. "No passwords." casual. "Seeker?" checking your ID. "You're on the list." waving you through, a small nod.
S04.eleven: [casual] No passwords. ... [checking your ID] Seeker? ... [waving you in] You're on the list.

S05.direction: "Pick a look." is a light invitation. You land on a skull: he's dryly amused, a little flattered.
S05.eleven: Pick a look. ... ... [dryly amused] Hey, that's my look.

S06.direction: "Pick a habit." crisp. He reads what you typed: "Every day?" one eyebrow up. "I give it three days." is a seasoned bookie setting odds against you: dry, friendly, completely sure of himself. (The "3 days" option is on screen as he says it; you pick 7.)
S06.eleven: Pick a habit. ... [skeptical] Every day? ... [dry, knowing] I give it three days.

S07.direction: Now it's a dare, straight after his bet: quick and delighted, leaning on "money".

S08.direction: "Then sign it." matter-of-fact. "Like a contract." mock-solemn and lawyerly, every syllable placed.
S08.eleven: Then sign it. ... [mock-solemn] Like a contract.

S09.direction: Right after his seal slams down: satisfied and final, playground-smug.

S10.direction: "Now." leans in, lower and closer. "Bring your friends." opens up warmly: this is the good part.

S11.direction: Two equal beats, like dealing cards. The second a touch lower.

S12.direction: Fond exasperation as Arjun finally opens the invite. "Arjun." has a sigh in it. "Finally." is dry: he's been waiting all evening. Teasing, never mean.

S13.direction: Quick, impressed aside: Dev was in before anyone asked.

S14.direction: Low and slow, savouring the pot.
S14.eleven: [low, savouring it] Four thousand on the table.

S15.direction: A brisk list in three beats. Then "I check every one." quieter and closer: a smiling threat.
S15.eleven: Two photos a day. ... Random gesture. ... [quietly, a smiling threat] I check every one.

S16.direction: LOCKED close-up. The catchphrase, flat as a table: two words a hair apart, falling. No smile.

S17.direction: Thumbs up, but grudging: he didn't expect this. "Not bad." is the most praise you'll get from him.

S18.direction: The music drops out. Quiet and close, building suspense, like a late-night radio host. (Your phone reads 0h 08m left.)
S18.eleven: [quietly] Day two. ... [hushed, suspenseful] Eight minutes left.

S19.direction: Gossip out of the side of his mouth. Voiced, not whispered.
S19.eleven: [gossiping, under his breath] Arjun's still on the couch.

S20.direction: A veteran bookie quoting odds: dry and certain. Then leave the silence for the countdown.
S20.eleven: [dry, like a bookie] Three to one he misses.

S21.direction: "Miss a day..." slow and ominous, then the payoff quicker and satisfied. Project over the drop.
S21.eleven: [ominous] Miss a day... [satisfied] and your friends split your stake.

S22.direction: LOCKED close-up. The mask slips: "Honestly?" a low confession. Then "I love this part." is deep, genuine delight, a low laugh riding on the words. Big, but never squeaky.
S22.eleven: [lowering his voice] Honestly? ... [a low, delighted laugh in his voice] I love this part.

S23.direction: "Blurry photo?" mock-curious. "Your friends decide." a shrug, hands off.

S24.direction: He reads the verdict, then can't hide it: no payday this time. "Shame." is a tiny, dry sulk with a smile in it.

S25.direction: The payoff of his bet: genuinely impressed, a little surprised. Then "Collect." cool and clipped.

S26.direction: "Arjun?" a glance. "He'll be back." knowing and teasing: he's sure Arjun returns (and pays again).

S27.direction: A hustler's pitch picking up speed: tempting question, proud reveal, light throwaway, then a door shutting.
S27.eleven: [tempting] Want a bigger table? ... [proud] Bounties. ... [quick, light] Free to join. ... [flat] Miss once, you're out.

S28.direction: Even and satisfied, a croupier pushing the chips across.
S28.eleven: [matter-of-fact] Last ones standing split the pool.

S29.direction: Closer and quieter (the music drops). Plain fact, then a dare with a smile: he wants you to win.
S29.eleven: [plainly] Your kept rate is public. ... [a friendly dare] Make it worth reading.

S30.direction: His arc closes over the wall of screens. Softer and closer: he admits he was wrong about you. Then the grin comes straight back for the punchline.
S30.eleven: [softly, admitting it] I gave you three days. ... [the grin comes back] Don't let it go to your head.

phrases.caption: Don't let it go to your head.

S31.direction: LOCKED: the end card types the tagline word by word on his voice. Slow, clean, weighty; the dry edge comes back on "Or pay your friends."
S31.eleven: [slow and clear] Keep your word. ... [dry, with weight] Or pay your friends.

S32.direction: A confident, warm sign-off. "Kept." short and crisp. "On Seeker." light. "October sixteenth." with a smile. Finish down.
S32.eleven: [confident] Kept. ... On Seeker. ... [warm, with a smile] October sixteenth.

S33.direction: The last word, low and close as he points at you: half threat, half joke, all grin. The wink follows.
S33.eleven: [low, with a grin] I'll be watching.
